1	# Nxeon — Pre-launch QA audit
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-25 · **Scope:** customer portal, admin portal, backend (`lib/**`, `worker/**`, `app/api/**`)
4	**Method:** source review, read-only inspection of the live `nxeon` database, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and
5	cross-checking the Proxmox perl source on this host. Nothing in this audit modified code, services, or data.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Executive summary
10	
11	### The single most dangerous issue
12	
13	**Any customer who can afford the cheapest email plan can take over another customer's email domain,
14	reset the password on their live mailboxes, and read and send mail as them.**
15	
16	`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:254-257` scopes the "one subscription per domain" check to the *caller*:
17	
18	```ts
19	const dupe = await db.emailSubscription.findFirst({
20	  where: { userId: user.id, domainName: name, status: { not: "CANCELLED" } },
21	});
22	```
23	
24	There is no check that another user already holds that domain, no `@@unique` on
25	`EmailSubscription.domainName` (`prisma/schema.prisma:604`), no `@unique` on `Mailbox.address`
26	(`:623`), and no `sub.verified` gate on any mailbox mutation. Every Mailcow call is keyed by the
27	**address string** on one shared Mailcow instance, so `resetMailboxPassword` (`:706`) rewrites the
28	password of whatever real mailbox that string names — and hands the plaintext back to the caller.
29	
30	Mailcow is configured in production (`MAILCOW_API_URL` + `MAILCOW_API_KEY` are both set), and the live
31	DB holds two active subscriptions with real mailboxes — including `admin@revsports.ca`, the platform's
32	own `BASE_DOMAIN`, which receives Nxeon's own password-reset mail. This is exploitable today, by any
33	signed-up user, in three clicks. Full detail in **P0-1**.
34	
35	### Go / no-go
36	
37	**NO-GO for paying customers.** Fix P0-1 through P0-8 first; they are the launch blockers.
38	
39	This is not a verdict on the codebase's quality — much of it is genuinely better than typical for this
40	stage. The wallet ledger is atomic and race-safe (`lib/wallet.ts` conditional `updateMany`, CAS on
41	`expiresAt` in every renewal path). Ownership checks are present and correct on **all 20+ mutating
42	server actions and all 35 API routes** — two independent passes found no IDOR in the server/domain/
43	volume/website/database/file surfaces. `lib/ssh-exec.ts` is a reject-don't-sanitize allowlist with
44	mandatory timeouts and secrets confined to STDIN; **no command injection was found anywhere**, and
45	that was looked for hard. Disk shrink is blocked at four independent layers. `qm destroy` is reachable
46	only through a `Server` row. Job claiming is atomic. GDPR deletion re-validates server-side.
47	
48	The problems are concentrated in four themes:
49	
50	* **9 P0s.** One live cross-tenant email takeover; one unauthenticated 2FA-verification endpoint; two
51	  paths that silently destroy customer volumes; a Stripe flow that can take money and provision
52	  nothing; proration that overcharges by up to $379; refunds that are untraceable and non-idempotent;
53	  a suspension path that permanently deletes a *paid-up* customer's VM; and a "Daily auto-backups"
54	  add-on that never produces a single backup.
55	* **A large "furniture" surface — the dominant defect class in this codebase.** ~18 admin settings are
56	  written to the DB and read by nothing (the dunning controls, the referral reward, the domain markup —
57	  which displays 0% while customers are charged 25%), and the customer portal has a matching set:
58	  notification preferences, SSL auto-renew, WHOIS privacy, custom nameservers, registrar lock, team
59	  permissions, affiliate tiers, mail Reply-To and the API `write` scope are all persisted, all
60	  confirmed with a green "Saved", and all read by nothing. **Every one of these tells the user a
61	  guarantee is in force when it is not.**
62	* **Whole features that cannot work today**: plan downgrades (blocked by a guard no live plan pair can
63	  satisfy), coupons (redemption UI hidden whenever Stripe is on), bandwidth metering (and therefore the
64	  entire abuse-detection subsystem built on it), 4 of the 5 one-click apps, and game settings.
65	* **One availability landmine**: a single hung job wedges the entire platform's queue, forever.
66	
67	A useful signal for triage: the team already knows how to handle an unfinished feature correctly.
68	`components/customer/AutoRecharge.tsx` is deliberately **not rendered**, with the reason documented in
69	`app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:11-15` — *"the feature is unwired … so we don't expose it and promise
70	something that does nothing."* That is exactly the right call. Roughly 25 findings below are the same
71	situation handled the other way.
72	
73	**Counts:** P0 · 9 · P1 · 42 · P2 · 19 · P3 · 15
74	
75	---
76	
77	# P0 — money and data
78	
79	## P0-1. Cross-tenant email domain takeover — live and exploitable today
80	
81	**Files:** `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:254-257`, `:491-539`, `:684-722`, `:81-122`;
82	`prisma/schema.prisma:600-626`; `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:88-94`
83	
84	Four defects compose into a full takeover:
85	
86	1. **Caller-scoped duplicate check** (`:254-257`) — a second user can claim a domain another customer
87	   already has a subscription for.
88	2. **No DB-level uniqueness** — `EmailSubscription.domainName` and `Mailbox.address` are both plain
89	   `String`. Nothing stops the second claim.
90	3. **`sub.verified` is never checked before any mailbox mutation.** `addMailbox` (`:499`) gates only
91	   on `sub.userId === user.id`, and its address-collision check (`:514`) only looks at
92	   `sub.mailboxes` — the *attacker's own* subscription's mailboxes. It cannot see the victim's.
93	4. **Mailcow is addressed by string, not by an identifier we own.**
94	
95	**Exploit** (attacker = any signed-up user with enough balance for the cheapest email plan):
96	
97	1. `orderEmailHosting("victim.com", planId)` → accepted (`external: true, verified: false`).
98	2. `addMailbox(subId, "ceo")` → row created with `address = "ceo@victim.com"`. If the mailbox already
99	   exists in Mailcow the create fails and the row lands `FAILED` — **but the row persists with the
100	   victim's address.**
101	3. `resetMailboxPassword(mailboxId)` → `:706` `mcSetMailboxPassword(mailbox.address, password)`
102	   rewrites the password on the **real, live** mailbox and returns the plaintext to the attacker.
103	   Full IMAP/SMTP/webmail: read the victim's mail, and send as them with Nxeon's SPF/DKIM alignment.
104	   `resolveMailbox` (`lib/mail/imap.ts:90`) also resolves it, so the built-in webmail works.
105	
106	**Variants, same root cause:**
107	* **Destruction** — `removeMailbox` (`:588`) `mcDeleteMailbox(mailbox.address)` deletes the victim's
108	  mailbox and all stored mail; the error is swallowed and the attacker's row is dropped.
109	* **Denial of service** — `setMailboxSuspended` (`:617`).
110	* **Silent interception** — `ownedDomains()` (`lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:88-94`) treats an
111	  **unverified** subscription as proof of domain control, so `mcAddAlias` can forward inbound mail.
112	* **Spoofing any domain** — `:95-98` calls `mcCreateDomain(domain)` for any claimed name, making the
113	  shared Mailcow authoritative for domains the attacker doesn't own. Independent IP-reputation risk.
114	
115	**Fix.** (a) Add `@@unique([domainName])` on `EmailSubscription` (excluding CANCELLED via a partial
116	index or a status-aware guard) and `@unique` on `Mailbox.address`. (b) Make the duplicate check global,
117	not caller-scoped. (c) Refuse **every** mailbox/alias mutation unless `sub.verified === true`, and
118	require DNS proof-of-control before verification for `external` domains. (d) Before any Mailcow write,
119	re-assert that the address's domain belongs to a verified subscription owned by the caller.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## P0-2. `verifyTotpForUser` is an unauthenticated, unthrottled 2FA oracle
124	
125	**File:** `lib/actions-2fa.ts:50-71` (file is `"use server"` at `:1`)
126	
127	```ts
128	export async function verifyTotpForUser(userId: string, code: string): Promise<boolean> {
129	  const user = await db.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
130	  ...
131	```
132	
133	Every export of a `"use server"` module is a registered, callable server action. This one takes an
134	arbitrary `userId`, performs **no authentication, no ownership check and no rate limit**, returns a
135	raw boolean, and **mutates state** — a matching backup code is consumed and deleted (`:62-63`).
136	
137	`login` (`lib/actions.ts:157`) is throttled to 10 attempts per 15 min per email+IP. Calling this action
138	directly bypasses that entirely: unlimited TOTP and backup-code guessing against a named account.
139	Victim `userId`s are readily obtainable — `inviteMember` (`lib/actions-teams.ts:110`) creates a
140	Membership **without the invitee's consent**, and `app/dashboard/team/page.tsx:42-47` then hands the
141	attacker every co-member's `userId` and email.
142	
143	The action's ID does not currently appear in any client chunk, so it is obscure — but obscurity is not
144	a boundary, and the codebase already treats exactly this threat as real elsewhere
145	(`assertInternalGrowthCaller`, `lib/actions-growth.ts:11-30`).
146	
147	**Fix.** Move `verifyTotpForUser` into a plain (non-`"use server"`) module imported by the login
148	action, or gate it behind a short-lived signed "password stage passed" token plus the same rate limit
149	as `login`.
150	
151	---
152	
153	## P0-3. Stripe pays, nothing is provisioned — the webhook consumes the fulfilment signal
154	
155	**Files:** `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:19-22`, `app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:27-94`,
156	`lib/stripe.ts:192-244`
157	
158	`creditCheckoutSession()` is idempotent via a `UNIQUE(stripeSessionId)` index and returns `true` only
159	for the caller that actually inserted the row. That boolean is the *only* signal that a session is
160	newly paid — and the confirm route gates all three fulfilment actions on it:
161	
162	```ts
163	// app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:27-44
164	const credited = await creditCheckoutSession(sessionId);
165	const order = await getCheckoutOrderIntent(sessionId);
166	if (order) {
167	  if (credited) { ...placeOrder(user, order.intent)... }
168	  return NextResponse.redirect(`${base}/dashboard/servers`);   // ← silent no-op path
169	}
170	```
171	
172	The webhook calls the same function and throws the result away:
173	
174	```ts
175	// app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:21
176	await creditCheckoutSession(session.id);
177	```
178	
179	**Failure scenario 1 (race).** Customer completes Checkout for a $249 annual Max VPS. Stripe fires
180	`checkout.session.completed` and redirects the browser at essentially the same instant. The webhook's
181	insert wins; the confirm request gets `P2002` → `credited === false` → line 44 redirects to
182	`/dashboard/servers`, which is empty. $249 charged, $249 in the wallet, no server, no error, no
183	notification, no admin alert.
184	
185	**Failure scenario 2 (deterministic, 100% reproducible).** Customer pays, then closes the tab / loses
186	connectivity before `success_url` resolves. The confirm route is never called at all. Identical
187	outcome. Stripe's own guidance is explicit that a redirect must not be the fulfilment trigger.
188	
189	The same defect applies verbatim to paid **upgrades** (`confirm/route.ts:52-70`) and paid **disk
190	expansions** (`:76-94`) — card charged, wallet credited, `RESIZE`/`DISK_EXPAND` job never queued.
191	
192	Nothing reconciles this: `grep -rl stripe worker/` returns nothing. Both keys are set in `.env`, so
193	this is live.
194	
195	**Fix.** Extract a shared `fulfilCheckoutSession(sessionId)` called by **both** the webhook and the
196	confirm route, made idempotent on its own marker (a `FulfilledSession` row, or a unique
197	`Job.stripeSessionId`) rather than on the wallet-credit side effect. Add a worker sweep that lists
198	sessions `paid` in the last 24h carrying `nxeonOrder`/`nxeonResize`/`nxeonDiskExpand` metadata with no
199	corresponding Server/Job and fulfils or alerts.
200	
201	---
202	
203	## P0-4. `BACKUP_RESTORE` permanently destroys attached block-storage volumes
204	
205	**Files:** `worker/restore.ts:116-120`, `lib/actions-server-ops.ts:116-147`
206	
207	```ts
208	// worker/restore.ts:116-120
209	const restoreUpid = await conn.post(`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu`, { vmid, archive: volid, force: 1 });
210	```
211	
212	There is **no volume guard anywhere** in `worker/restore.ts` or the calling action — both were read in
213	full; neither mentions volumes. Confirmed against the hypervisor source on this box:
214	
215	* `/usr/share/perl5/PVE/QemuServer.pm:7751` — `destroy_vm(...) if -f $vmcfgfn;` with the comment
216	  *"avoid zombie disks when restoring over an existing VM -> cleanup first"*.
217	* `/usr/share/perl5/PVE/QemuServer.pm:1877-1882` — `destroy_vm` uses `include_unused => 1` and frees
218	  **every** volume owned by that vmid, `unusedN` entries included.
219	
220	**Failure scenario, on live data.** Server `ggjgjhgjghh` (vmid 102, `autoBackup: true`) has volume
221	"size 60" `ATTACHED` as `vmdata:vm-102-disk-1`. The customer restores any backup taken before the
222	volume was attached → `qmrestore --force` → `destroy_vm` frees `vm-102-disk-1` → the customer's data is
223	gone. `Volume.diskName` still points at the dead volid and **billing continues**.
224	
225	The reinstall path has an explicit, well-reasoned guard for exactly this hazard
226	(`worker/index.ts:416-444`). Restore, which does the same thing to the same vmid, has none.
227	
228	**Fix.** Apply the reinstall guard to restore: refuse `BACKUP_RESTORE` while any `Volume` is pinned to
229	the server (`serverId` set, regardless of status), at both the action and the worker handler.
230	
231	---
232	
233	## P0-5. Same-OS reinstall wipes a DETACHED-but-pinned volume — guard asymmetry
234	
235	**Files:** `lib/actions.ts:465`, `worker/index.ts:428-430`, `worker/index.ts:357-360`,
236	`worker/volumes.ts:240`, `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:112`
237	
238	`volumeDetach` deliberately keeps `serverId` so the volume can be re-attached; it only flips status
239	(`worker/volumes.ts:240`). The **OS-change** path counts *all* pinned volumes and is correct:
240	
241	```ts
242	// lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:112
243	const pinnedVolumes = await db.volume.count({ where: { serverId } });
244	```
245	
246	The **same-OS "Reinstall"** path counts only `ATTACHED`, at both layers:
247	
248	```ts
249	// lib/actions.ts:465          and      worker/index.ts:428-430
250	db.volume.count({ where: { serverId, status: "ATTACHED" } })
251	```
252	
253	then:
254

460	never settles. Compare the correct pattern at `lib/ssh-exec.ts:121-130`, `worker/ssl.ts:83-90`,

652	"Port-forward sync" and "Improvement agent". Nothing is probed. The page header (`:44`) reads *"Every
653	background system actually running on this platform — no vapourware."*

655	*Failure:* `nxeon-worker` is stopped or crash-looping (see **P1-1**) and this page still shows four

657	(`lib/monitoring.ts:262-289`) and doesn't use it here.
658	
659	## P1-13. The bulk action bar reports success counts it never received
660	
661	**Files:** `components/admin/BulkTable.tsx:66-75`, `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:181-225`
662	
663	```ts
664	await action.run(ids);
665	setMsg(`${action.label}: ${ids.length} row${…} done.`);
666	```
667	
668	The return value is discarded. `bulkSuspendUsers` filters out `role: ADMIN` and the acting admin and
669	returns `{ suspended }`; `bulkVoidInvoices` skips PAID invoices and returns `{ voided, skipped }`.
670	
671	*Failure:* on `/admin/users` the admin selects 5 staff accounts and clicks Suspend → banner reads
672	**"Suspend: 5 rows done."** while zero were suspended. On `/admin/invoices`, selecting 20 invoices of
673	which 15 are PAID reports "Void: 20 rows done." when 5 were voided.
674	
675	## P1-14. Plan downgrades cannot succeed for any customer — the feature is inert
676	
677	**Files:** `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:163`, `components/customer/ResizeDown.tsx:88-96`
678	
679	The downgrade guard requires the target plan's disk to be `>=` the current plan's. Cross-checking the
680	**live** plan catalogue, every active plan is strictly ordered by both price and disk (Starter 25 GB /
681	$8.99 · Standard 50 GB / $12.99 · Pro 80 GB / $20.99 · Max 120 GB / $32.99), so there is **not one
682	valid downgrade pair**.
683	
684	*Failure:* a Max customer opens the "Downsize your plan" card, sees three cheaper plans rendered at
685	40% opacity with every button `disabled` and the submit button permanently greyed out. The empty-state
686	copy ("You're already on the smallest plan") only fires when there are no cheaper plans at all, so it
687	never shows. The feature is shipped, prominent, and impossible to use.
688	
689	## P1-15. `ResizeDown`'s displayed credit uses a third, different formula from the server
690	
691	**Files:** `components/customer/ResizeDown.tsx:49-59` vs `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:176-183`
692	
693	Client: `(vpsTermPriceCents(old) − vpsTermPriceCents(new)) × remainingFraction`, clamped to one term.
694	Server: `(old.priceCents − new.priceCents) × remainingMonths`, undiscounted and unclamped.
695	
696	For Max→Standard with 364 days left on an annual term the customer is shown **$215.41** and credited
697	**$239.16**. This directly violates the invariant the codebase states for every other money path
698	("the split the customer SEES is byte-for-byte the split that gets CHARGED",
699	`lib/wallet-split.ts:1-4`). Currently masked by P1-14.
700	
701	## P1-16. Detach hot-unplugs a mounted filesystem from a running VM
702	
703	**Files:** `lib/actions-volumes.ts:147-154`, `worker/volumes.ts:236`, `worker/product-renewals.ts:433-435`
704	
705	The only guard is `volume.status !== "ATTACHED"`. There is no `server.status` check — conspicuous,
706	because `attachVolume` has one (`lib/actions-volumes.ts:124`). The worker issues a live SCSI unplug
707	with no `fsfreeze`, `sync`, or guest-agent unmount; provision never sets `hotplug`
708	(`worker/index.ts:284-303`), so Proxmox's default `disk,network,usb` applies.
709	
710	*Failure:* volume mounted at `/var/lib/mysql`; customer clicks Detach (UI says *"Data is preserved"*);
711	the device vanishes mid-write → journal abort / InnoDB corruption. The same primitive fires **with no
712	human involved** from billing: `worker/product-renewals.ts:433-435` queues `VOLUME_DETACH` on an
713	overdue volume attached to a running VM.
714	
715	## P1-17. Re-attach with a lost `diskName` hands back a blank disk and orphans the data
716	
717	**Files:** `worker/volumes.ts:166`, `:199`, `:231`, `:240-248`; `worker/index.ts:432-436`
718	
719	```ts
720	const source = volume.diskName ? volume.diskName : `${storage}:${volume.sizeGB}`;
721	```
722	
723	No "was this attached before?" check. `worker/index.ts:432-436` proves null-`diskName` ATTACHED volumes
724	occur in production, and `worker/volumes.ts:172-175` documents the race that causes it.
725	
726	*Failure:* volume V (500 GB of data) has `diskName === null`. Detach → `:231` `if (server?.vmid &&
727	volume.diskName)` is false so nothing is unplugged, but `:240` flips to DETACHED and `:242-248`
728	notifies *"data are preserved."* Re-attach → line 166 creates a **brand-new empty 500 GB disk** and
729	`:199` overwrites `diskName`. The customer sees an unformatted disk; the real zvol is orphaned with no
730	DB reference.
731	
732	## P1-18. `Node.natChain` / `subnetPrefix` are validated, stored, and ignored by the worker
733	
734	**Files:** `lib/actions-nodes.ts:21, :128-131, :174-200`; `worker/network.ts:7, :32-54`;
735	`app/admin/nodes/new/page.tsx:24-25`
736	
737	`natChain` is documented as *"the iptables chain the worker rebuilds from the DB"* and is enforced
738	globally unique. But `worker/network.ts:7` hardcodes `process.env.NXEON_NAT_CHAIN ?? "NXEON_FWD"`, and
739	`syncPortForwards()` selects **every** server regardless of node and DNATs them all into that one
740	chain. `Node.natChain` has no consumer anywhere.
741	
742	*Failure:* admin registers node-2 via `/admin/nodes/new` and provisions a VM there (guest
743	`10.20.1.101`). The worker flushes `NXEON_FWD` **on the primary host** and adds a DNAT to an address
744	that host cannot route. `NXEON_FWD_N2` is never created on node-2. Every node-2 VM has dead SSH while
745	`/admin/nodes` shows the node green/ONLINE.
746	
747	*Compounding:* `updateNode` (`:174-200`) lets an admin change `subnetPrefix`, `ipStart/ipEnd`,
748	`natChain` and `bridge` on a node that already has servers — no `_count.servers` guard (only
749	`deleteNode:292` has one). Editing the subnet on the live primary makes `lib/ipam.ts:168` stop seeing
750	existing leases, and the next provision hands out an IP already in use.

752	## P1-19. Team RBAC (`Membership.areas`) is computed, stored, and never enforced
753	
754	**Files:** `lib/team-guard.ts:16`, `lib/team-areas.ts:71, :103`, `lib/actions-teams.ts:195`,
755	`app/dashboard/team/page.tsx:48`

758	referenced only from inside `team-guard.ts` itself; `memberCanAccessHref` is never called.
759	`setMemberAreas` writes the field, the UI renders it, nothing reads it back.

761	Not currently exploitable — org membership grants no resource access anywhere (verified: no query

763	`["invoices"]` gets a UI that says the restriction is in force when it is not, and the moment
764	org-shared resources land this becomes a live hole.

767	
768	**Verified by mapping every `invoiceCreateData` / `createInvoice` call site.** Invoices are created for
769	VPS orders, VPS renewals, resizes, disk expansions, domain transfers-in, domain *auto*-renewals and

781	expense — and finds nothing. Twelve months later the auto-renewal produces one, so the gap looks like
782	a bug rather than a policy. Same for anyone buying a game server or a volume.

784	## P1-21. `maybeRewardReferral` can be self-invoked to mint referral credit with no payment
785	
786	**Files:** `lib/actions-growth.ts:258`, guard at `:25-30`
787	
788	`assertInternalGrowthCaller` permits an action-dispatched call when `real.id === userId`. But the
789	function's own contract (`:256`) is "callable from `topUp` / `orderServer` **after a paid action**." A
790	user calling it on their own id skips the payment entirely: both they and their referrer are credited
791	`REFERRAL_REWARD_CENTS` (`:277-290`). `referralRewardedAt` caps it at once per account, so the abuse
792	shape is farming — N self-registered accounts under one referral code, each self-calling, yields
793	N × $5 to the referrer for $0.

795	---

802	`components/customer/cpanel/shared.tsx:65-67`; `lib/actions-apps.ts:201`

3769	## Known gaps — the honest inventory
3770	
3771	Verified against the tree at the time of writing. Several agents edit this repo concurrently, so
3772	re-check anything before you rely on it. Classification:
3773	
3774	- **WORKS** — verified end to end.
3775	- **SIMULATED** — produces a fabricated result.
3776	- **UNVERIFIED SUCCESS** — does real work but reports success without checking it.
3777	- **SAVED-BUT-UNREAD** — written by a UI, consumed by nothing.
3778	- **DEAD** — implemented, never called.
3779	- **PARTIAL** — real but incomplete or overstated.
3780	
3781	### Fixed since the last audit — verified, do not re-report these
3782	
3783	| Item | Evidence |
3784	|---|---|
3785	| **Stripe could take payment and provision nothing** | `FulfilledSession` + one shared `fulfilCheckoutSession` called by **both** the redirect and the webhook. `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`, `app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:27`, `webhook/route.ts:34` |
3786	| **SSL wrote ACTIVE rows with invented expiries** | Fall-through throws (`worker/ssl.ts:692`); expiry is the observed `notAfter` (`:434`, `:303`), and issuance throws if it cannot be parsed (`:311`). `ENABLE_REAL_SSL=1` is set |
3787	| **Migration reported success with domains dark** | `judgeMigrationOutcome` (`migrate-real.ts:2262`) scored against the **source's own** vhosts; `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` persisted (`migrate.ts:412`); UI renders amber (`MigrationWizard.tsx:1396`) |
3788	| **Admin showed 0% domain markup while charging 25%** | Read at `lib/registrar.ts:89`; default corrected to `"25"` with a warning comment (`lib/settings.ts:52-56`) |
3789	| **Auto-suspend kill switch read by nothing** | `auto_suspend_enabled` gates three paths: `worker/billing.ts:143`, `:897`, `:924`, `:1316` |
3790	| **Dunning day settings read by nothing** | `dunningConfig()` reads all three from Settings (`worker/billing.ts:139-143`) |
3791	| **Game settings claimed "applied" with nothing written** | Throws outside sandbox with an explanation (`worker/game-config.ts:86`) |
3792	| **An admin/abuse suspension deleted a paid-up customer's server** | Both termination and auto-unsuspend scope to `suspendReason: "UNPAID"` (`worker/billing.ts:1333`, `lib/actions.ts:690`) |
3793	| **A customer's backup could delete the platform's DR archives** | Three layers: structural (`/tank/backup/platform` is outside every PVE storage), chokepoint (`deleteBackup` fails closed), marker+registry. `lib/proxmox.ts:403-437` |
3794	| **"Daily backups" add-on read by nothing** | Bridged at the point of sale — `lib/order.ts:258` |
3795	| **Proration over- and under-charged** | One shared `lib/proration.ts` for charge, credit and display |
3796	| **Cross-tenant email-domain takeover** | Global duplicate check (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:269`) + `Mailbox.address @unique` (`schema.prisma:674`) |
3797	| **2FA verification was a public brute-force oracle** | Moved to the plain module `lib/totp-verify.ts` |
3798	| **Volumes were never formatted or mounted; detach had no safety check** | Format-on-first-use, fstab by UUID, and a worker-side refusal that names the dependents (`worker/volumes.ts:601`, `:554`, `:1189`) |
3799	| **Reinstall could wipe an attached volume** | `worker/index.ts:428-448` |
3800	| **Refunds guessed their Stripe target and could double-refund** | Bound to `invoiceId`, `Invoice.refundedCents` tracked, `REFUNDED` set (`lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:61`, `:179`) |
3801	| **Auto-reply / forwarding were store-only** | Real Mailcow sieve, pushed before the DB write, status read back from the live script |
3802	| **Display name / Reply-To saved and never used** | Applied at `lib/actions-mail.ts:468-487` |
3803	| **`Membership.areas` was a fake restriction** | The control was removed and the customer is told the truth |
3804	| **Bandwidth columns were never written** | Metering landed in `lib/bandwidth.ts` + `worker/monitor.ts:205`, wired inside `monitorSweep` at `:456` |
3805	| **One-click apps reported ACTIVE without installing anything** | Rewritten: every app declares what its install proves, and `verifyServing()` HTTP-probes the domain and matches application markers in the **body**. An exit code of 0 is never accepted as proof; a failed probe **fails the job** with the real HTTP result rather than downgrading to "needs setup". `worker/apps.ts:46-69`, `:760-776` |
3806	| **SSL renewal / reconcile sweeps shipped as dead code** | Registered — `worker/index.ts:18` now imports `sslSweep` and `:1098` calls it on the loop (commit `2f22115`) |
3807	| **The billing page presented a partial bandwidth period as authoritative** | Adopted `bwUsageView`, which reports the period the meter actually covers — `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:11`, `:68`, `:73` |
3808	| **Coupon codes on card top-ups were silently ignored** | The route now **refuses** with an explanation and clears the cookie in the same response, so the retry succeeds — `app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts:29-54`. It also documents why Stripe `discounts` are the wrong instrument for a wallet top-up (they reduce `amount_total`, hence the credit, by the same cents) |
3809	| **Automatic abuse suspension did not tag `suspendReason`** | `worker/abuse.ts:265` now sets `"ABUSE"`, so billing will not delete the VM and paying cannot lift it (`:288`) |
3810	| **Proxmox `:8006` and host SSH were world-open in the firewall script** | `scripts/firewall.nft:120` defines `ADMIN_PORTS = { 22, 8006 }`, accepted only from the admin address sets (`:190-191`). ⚠ **The script is fixed; the live ruleset is not — see gap 2** |
3811	| **Plan downgrade offered options that all errored** | commit `e208290` |
3812	
3813	### Still not true — ranked by what it would cost a customer or admin
3814	
3815	> **This list was re-verified line by line at the end of the writing pass, and four items moved out of
3816	> it while the document was being written** (one-click app verification, the SSL sweep registration,
3817	> the bandwidth view, and the coupon refusal). Several agents commit to this tree continuously. Re-run
3818	> the grep before you rely on any entry.
3819	
3820	**1. There is no UI to save a card, so renewal auto-charge can never fire.** *DEAD.*
3821	The engine is real and wired (`worker/billing.ts:28-43` imports 13 symbols from `lib/stripe-cards`),
3822	but `lib/actions-payment-method.ts` — `startCardSetup` `:46`, `finalizeCardSetup` `:72`,
3823	`removeSavedCard` `:101`, `settleOutstanding` `:127` — has **zero callers** in `app/` or
3824	`components/`. Every renewal is therefore wallet-only, and a customer with an empty wallet goes
3825	straight to grace → suspend: precisely the outcome the dunning engine was built to prevent. This is
3826	the single highest-value wiring job outstanding.
3827	
3828	**2. The hardened firewall is in the file, not in the kernel.** *NOT APPLIED.*
3829	`scripts/firewall.nft` has been rewritten to restrict the two administrative ports —
3830	`define ADMIN_PORTS = { 22, 8006 }` (`:120`), accepted only from `@nxeon_admin_v4`/`@nxeon_admin_v6`
3831	(`:190-191`) — and the comment at `:21-35` explains why: a successful login on `:8006` is
3832	*"not 'a server gets hacked', it is 'the hosting company ends'"*. But the **live** ruleset still reads:
3833	
3834	```
3835	tcp dport { 22, 80, 443, 8006, 8080, 8443 } accept
3836	```
3837	
3838	So Proxmox's web UI and host SSH are reachable from the internet right now. Populate the admin sets and
3839	apply with `scripts/firewall-safe-apply.sh` (it has a rollback timer — do not `nft -f` by hand over an
3840	SSH session you cannot afford to lose).
3841	
3842	**3. Game auto-update cannot fail.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS — runs unattended every 6 hours.*
3843	`worker/game-update.ts:60` returns `set -e; ${steam}${restart}; true`. steamcmd is `|| true` (`:51`)
3844	and skipped entirely when absent; every restart branch is `|| true` (`:59`); the command ends `; true`.
3845	The remote command **cannot** exit non-zero, so `:134` always fires *"The latest server update was
3846	applied and the service was restarted."* `worker/apps.ts` is now the model for how to fix this — it
3847	proves the outcome with `verifyServing()` and fails the job with the real HTTP result.
3848	
3849	**4. Post-cutover TLS is never retried.** *DEAD.* `runPostCutoverTls` (`worker/migrate.ts:260`) is
3850	reached only via `payload.phase === "tls"`, and the enqueue line exists **only inside a comment**
3851	(`:258`) — a repo-wide grep for `phase: "tls"` returns that comment and nothing else.
3852	`pointMigrationDns` does not trigger it. So names that could not be issued at migration time — the
3853	normal case, since DNS has not moved yet — are never retried.
3854	`issueMigrationCertificates` (`migrate-real.ts:3236`) exists for exactly this and still effectively has
3855	no caller. Until it is wired, closing the loop means queueing the job by hand (see the migration
3856	re-run runbook).
3857	
3858	**5. Migration simulation still reports success when the flag is off.** *SIMULATED — dormant.*
3859	Unlike SSL and game-config, which now throw, `worker/migrate.ts:452` falls through to a synthetic
3860	branch that fabricates step results, writes `status: "DONE"` / `step: "Completed"` (`:533`) and
3861	notifies *"Migration to X completed"* (`:536`). Its sleep timings were written for the non-sandbox
3862	case. `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION=1` today, so it is dormant — **one lost `.env` line re-creates the
3863	original lie on the flagship feature.** The same fall-through shape applies to the four
3864	`ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` workers (`websites.ts:39`, `apps.ts:81`, `databases.ts:35`, `services.ts:34`).
3865	
3866	**6. Nxeon-registered domains get no mail DNS.** *PARTIAL — the UI promises otherwise.*
3867	`components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:261` tells the customer that a domain registered with Nxeon has
3868	*"its mail DNS managed for you — mailboxes go live automatically."* Nothing publishes
3869	MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC at name.com: `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:283` only ever adds A records. Their mail
3870	will not work, and the panel says it will.
3871	
3872	**7. `email_mx_host` and `email_spf_include` change nothing.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD — and the panel makes
3873	an explicit false claim about its own effect.* `components/admin/settings/GeneralPanel.tsx:26` says
3874	*"Shown in the customer business-email DNS setup panel"*; `:34` says *"Rendered as
3875	`v=spf1 include:<value> ~all`"*. Neither is true. The real values are hardcoded at
3876	`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:36` (`mail.nxeon.cloud`) and `:41` (`nxeon.cloud`), while the admin
3877	fields default to `mx.nxeon.email` and `_spf.nxeon.email` — so the panel makes correctly-configured
3878	mail look misconfigured, and editing either field does nothing.
3879	
3880	**8. Domain-ownership verification uses the wrong resolver.** *PARTIAL.*
3881	`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:5` imports the top-level `resolveTxt`/`resolveMx`, used at `:464` and
3882	`:474` — so verification runs against `/etc/resolv.conf` (OVH's cache), not the zone's authority. A
3883	customer who has just published `_nxeon-verify` can be told it is not there.
3884	`lib/mail/deliverability.ts` does it correctly and is the model to copy. The same bug is in
3885	`app/api/tools/dns/route.ts:35` (a `Resolver` with no `setServers`) and
3886	`app/api/tools/my-ip/route.ts:23` (`reverse` on the default resolver).
3887	
3888	**9. There is no PTR / reverse-DNS check anywhere.** *Missing.* `checkDeliverability` covers only
3889	`mx | spf | dkim | dmarc` (`lib/mail/deliverability.ts:41`) — despite the motivating incident being a
3890	*reverse* lookup. And the correct checker `checkEmailDeliverability`
3891	(`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:523`) has **no caller**, so there is no UI entry point at all.
3892	`components/admin/MailAnalytics.tsx:135-148`'s "DNS & DMARC" card is static prose, not a check.
3893	
3894	**10. Cloudflare connections cannot refresh.** *PARTIAL.* The working scope in `.env:39` omits
3895	`offline_access`, so Cloudflare issues no refresh token and every connection dies at `expiresAt`
3896	(`lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts:332` → `CF_RECONNECT`) with no re-auth prompt. Separately the **code
3897	default** scope (`:59`) is a value Cloudflare rejects, so any deploy that loses that env var
3898	reintroduces the "invalid scope" error a customer hit three times.
3899	
3900	**11. Backup monitoring is silent in the two cases that matter.** *PARTIAL.*
3901	`worker/monitor.ts:203` can only alert "stale" when `count > 0` **and** the listing was reachable. A
3902	server that has never been backed up, and a node whose backup listing failed (swallowed by a bare
3903	`catch {}` at `lib/monitoring.ts:203`), both produce **no alert** — which is exactly the failure
3904	`scripts/verify-restore.sh:7-11` was written after. Compounding it: the status JSON those scripts write
3905	"for `/admin/backups`" has **no reader and there is no such page**, and `verify-restore.sh` writes
3906	`"ok":true` even with a non-empty `warnings` field (`:122-127`), so a guest with no archive at all still
3907	reads as OK unless you look at `warnings`.
3908	
3909	**12. Off-site backups are inert.** *Not configured, honestly reported.* `/tank` is one pool in one
3910	chassis; `offsite.json` says `configured:false`. A chassis loss loses every backup, including the
3911	platform's own disaster-recovery set. Set `OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` or `OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET` in
3912	`/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env`.
3913	
3914	**13. A genuinely in-use volume cannot be force-detached.** *PARTIAL.* The worker supports an informed
3915	override via `payload.ackInUse` (`worker/volumes.ts:1147`) and the refusal notification tells the
3916	customer to *"confirm the forced detach in the dashboard"* — but **nothing sets it**: not
3917	`lib/actions-volumes.ts`, not `components/customer/Volumes.tsx`. The escape hatch exists only in the
3918	engine, and the notification points at a control that does not exist.
3919	
3920	**14. Volumes are not portable.** *PARTIAL — the framing is stronger than the code.*
3921	`lib/actions-volumes.ts:129` refuses attaching to any server other than `volume.serverId`, and detach
3922	only clears it when the disk did not stay behind (`worker/volumes.ts:1154`). Once a volume holds data it
3923	is effectively pinned to its first server.
3924	
3925	**15. "Restore failed — your server is unaffected" is false for restores.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS,
3926	inverted.* `components/customer/BackupControls.tsx:134` renders `{verb} failed — your server is
3927	unaffected` and `:147` adds *"No changes were made to your running server. You can safely try again."*
3928	— with `verbFor` (`:16`) returning `"Restore"` for `BACKUP_RESTORE`. By the time a restore fails,
3929	`worker/restore.ts:103-110` has already stopped the VM and begun overwriting its disk. **The most
3930	reassuring message in the product appears in its most destructive failure case.**
3931	
3932	**16. Game settings are switched off and the copy has not caught up.** *PARTIAL.*
3933	`ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` is unset, so every production save now fails loudly (`worker/game-config.ts:86`)
3934	— correct, but the feature is non-functional while
3935	`components/customer/GameSettings.tsx:72` still says *"Changes are queued and applied to the server"*
3936	and `:127` *"Settings queued for apply."* Even on the real path nothing reads back
3937	(`worker/game-config.ts:118-165`), and `:136` writes the `_appliedAt` marker even when
3938	`outcome.ok === false`.
3939	
3940	**17. The capacity gauge is a model, and it gates deploys.** *PARTIAL.*
3941	`lib/capacity.ts:15` uses `NXEON_HOST_RAM_MB ?? 64000` and the variable is unset, so the ceiling is a
3942	hardcoded assumption about this specific box. `capacitySnapshot()` sums **plan** RAM across servers on
3943	**all** nodes against that single-host ceiling, while the platform is multi-node. It is shown to
3944	customers at `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:34` and it **gates deploys** via `capacityCheck` (`:69`),
3945	so the number is load-bearing.

Two defaults changed so an empty `Setting` table renders byte-for-byte what it rendered before: `brand_tagline` is now the footer's exact former inline sentence, and `support_email` defaults to `support@nxeon.cloud` instead of `""` (a blank would have shipped an empty `mailto:`). `company_legal_name`/`company_address` stay blank-able — the seller block is omitted entirely rather than printing an empty "From". The three social env vars (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SOCIAL_*`, set nowhere) are gone; URLs without an `http(s)://` scheme fall back to the existing decorative `<span>` rather than emitting a relative href.

**`invoice_prefix` — wired.** `formatInvoiceNumber(number, prefix)` and async `invoiceBranding()` in `lib/invoices.ts`; `renderInvoiceHTML` takes an optional third `branding` arg defaulting to the platform values, so it stays synchronous and every existing caller still compiles. Wired at both invoice list pages, both detail pages and the download route. Visible change: `#00012` → `INV-00012`.

**`default_term` — made months-based (not deleted).** The enum was replaced with the month counts derived from `VPS_TERMS`, in three places that must agree: `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` (`"1"`), the `BillingPanel` select (options generated from `VPS_TERMS`, so adding a term surfaces it automatically) and the `TERMS` enum in `lib/actions-settings.ts`. `defaultTermMonths()` refuses anything not in `VPS_TERMS` and falls back to the first term. I chose this over deletion because the control is genuinely useful and the fix is mechanical — "quarterly" simply never existed, and biennial/triennial were unnameable. The live DB has no `default_term` row, so nothing needed migrating; a legacy `"monthly"` row is rejected on write and ignored on read.

**`default_plan_slug` — wired.** `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` resolves slug→id against the same `plans` array it passes down and hands the wizard `defaultPlanId`; the wizard's `Plan` type is untouched. A slug that no longer resolves (renamed/deactivated plan) degrades to the old first-plan-by-sortOrder behaviour instead of opening with nothing selected.

**`whois_privacy_default` — removed.** Taken out of the panel, out of the `domains` section of `lib/actions-settings.ts` (so it is not merely hidden from a hand-crafted POST) and out of `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS`. Privacy is unconditionally on and free at the registrar, registration never writes the column, and the wizard has only static "Included free" copy — honouring an OFF setting means building UI to decline a giveaway, which is a product decision, not a wiring gap.

**`tax_percent` — made honest, NOT charged.** I did not start charging tax; that is a legal/business decision and switching it on because a field existed would be the more serious error. The panel field now carries an explicit note: *"Display only — no charge path adds tax, so every invoice is still issued with Tax $0.00. Do not rely on this to collect VAT/GST."* The `taxRate()` docblock in `lib/tax.ts` states the same and names what must change (and that the panel note must be deleted in the same commit) if tax is ever really charged. I also added a one-line hint to the adjacent `currency` field, which is read but display-only with no FX — same lie shape, same panel.
